metadata.title: Florida Probate Explained: What Happens When Someone Dies Owning Real Estate?
metadata.author: Courtney Fricke
metadata.shortDescription:
Most people think probate is simply about inheriting Grandma's house.

In reality, probate sits at the center of some of the biggest ownership questions in Florida Real Estate.

Missing heirs.
Orphaned estates.
Vacant properties.
Family disputes.
Unknown owners.
Title problems.

In this episode of the Messy Money Podcast, I sit down with Florida probate attorney Al Nicoletti to break down what actually happens when someone dies owning Real Estate in Florida.

We discuss how ownership transfers after death, when probate is required, when it can be avoided, how to identify the right heirs, who actually has authority to sell, and what investors need to know before pursuing probate opportunities.

Whether you're an investor, Realtor, title professional, attorney, or simply trying to understand inherited property in Florida, this episode provides a practical roadmap for navigating probate and ownership issues.

What You'll Learn:
-What actually happens to ownership when someone dies in Florida
-When probate is required and when it can be avoided
-How trusts, Lady Bird Deeds, and joint ownership affect probate
-The first questions to ask when investigating an inherited property
-How to determine whether a will exists
-How to identify heirs when probate has never been opened
-Who actually has authority to sell inherited property
-The difference between heirs, beneficiaries, executors, and personal representatives
-When heirs can sign contracts before probate
-The difference between summary administration and formal administration
-Typical probate costs and timelines in Florida
-Common mistakes that derail probate deals
-How experienced operators solve complex ownership problems
